planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, or sow direct once soil has warmed; established clumps return reliably each spring.

directions: Dolores is a fine-textured chive selection bred for heavy production of edible lavender-purple flower heads alongside mild-flavored leaves. Sow seed shallowly in flats or direct in warm soil, then thin or transplant divisions into tight clumps. Shear the whole clump to an inch or two above ground several times through the growing season to keep leaves tender and discourage early flowering if leaf harvest is the priority. Leave some flower heads to mature for pollinator interest and striking color in the herb bed, and divide congested clumps every two to three years.

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant around last frost; parsley seed is slow and erratic to germinate, so keep soil consistently moist.

directions: Peione is an improved Giant-of-Italy-type flat-leaf parsley bred for larger, darker leaves on thick upright stems that stay clean and easy to harvest, plus partial resistance to downy mildew. Soak seed briefly before sowing to speed the notoriously slow germination, and keep the bed evenly moist until seedlings establish. Grow in rich, well-drained soil and side-dress lightly once plants reach several true leaves to sustain continuous leaf production. Harvest outer stems first, leaving the center to keep producing through the season and often into a mild winter.

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant around last frost; mulch well-drained beds to allow overwintering and an early spring flush in milder climates.

directions: Splendid is a high-yielding, organically produced Italian large-leaf parsley derived from Giant of Italy stock, prized for abundant dark green foliage and strong flavor. Pre-soak seed and sow into consistently moist soil, since germination is slow even under ideal conditions. Full sun and fertile, moisture-retentive soil push the fastest leaf growth; mulch in cold climates to protect crowns and the plants will often resume cutting in early spring. Clip outer leaf stalks regularly to encourage fresh regrowth from the center of the plant.

planting.note: Direct sow only, since the taproot resents disturbance; this compact selection suits containers and small-space succession sowing.

directions: Dwarf Lemon is a compact cilantro selection with the familiar grassy-citrus cilantro flavor layered with a noticeably stronger lemon aroma, making it popular for salsas and Southeast Asian dishes. Its small stature suits window boxes and tight raised-bed plantings where standard cilantro would sprawl. Sow directly and keep the seed bed evenly moist until germination, then thin crowded seedlings to let plants bush out. Harvest leaves continuously from the outside in, and sow a fresh short row every few weeks since the plant bolts quickly once the weather warms.

planting.note: Direct sow since the taproot resents transplanting; regional strain grown widely across South Asia for both fresh leaf and dried seed, known there as dhaniya.

directions: This regional South Asian coriander strain is prized for strongly scented, citrus-tinged dark green leaves used fresh in chutneys and curries, and for its dried seed used whole or ground as a core spice. Keep soil consistently moist for even germination, and cut leaves regularly to delay the inevitable bolt once days lengthen and warm. If seed is the goal, let a portion of the row flower and set seed heads, then cut and dry them fully before threshing. Leaves can even be harvested green and tender directly off a bolting plant, since the young seed heads are considered a delicacy in some regional cuisines.
